statement: A slug MUST be bounded at 60 characters. Truncation lands on a word boundary: cut to the bound, then drop everything from the last `-` onward. The single exception is a FIRST word that alone exceeds the bound -- there is no boundary to fall back to, so it is hard-cut, because a slug must be bounded.

input.question: how should the team decide whether to adopt a shared caching layer for the search path

cases.why: word-boundary truncation; the trailing partial word is dropped
single word longer than the bound; the only permitted mid-word cut
